content: Dari jalan besar, rumah kayu kami
hampir hilang di balik pepohonan yang
tumbuh sangat rapat.
= From the main road our wooden house
nearly vanishes behind trees grown
very close together.
pohon is one tree. pepohonan is the trees:
all of them at once, the green mass nobody
counts.
The shape is two things at the same time.
The first syllable is doubled, and the
whole of it is wrapped in pe-...-an.
pohon   ->  pepohonan   the trees
runtuh  ->  reruntuhan  the rubble
Most of them are simpler. A place word
plus -an is the spread of it.
darat    land   daratan   the mainland
laut     sea    lautan    the open sea
datar    level  dataran   a plain
pinggir  edge   pinggiran the outskirts
per-...-an and pe-...-an do the same work
on a larger scale:
air     water  perairan   a country's
own waters
gunung  mount  pegunungan a whole range
rumah   house  perumahan  an estate
One mountain is a gunung. Pegunungan is
what you see from the plane.
Kalau jalan desa rusak, warga kampung
memperbaikinya sendiri secara gotong
royong pada hari Minggu.
= If the village road breaks up, the
villagers repair it themselves by
communal labour on a Sunday.
gotong royong has no English. It is not
volunteering and it is not a working
party. It is the standing habit of a
village turning out together, unpaid, on
work that serves everyone: a road, a
drain, a neighbour's roof.
adat is the other one of its kind: custom,
and custom as law. Hukum adat settles
land and marriage where the state's law
does not reach.                       Press 1
The village runs on offices worth naming.
RT, RW     the lane and the block, run
by neighbours, not officials
kelurahan  the lowest ward office in a
town; lurah is its head
kecamatan  the district above it, under
a camat
Where the offices stop, the people begin.
musyawarah  talking a matter through
until everybody agrees
sesepuh     the elder with no post
whose word settles things
arisan      the monthly club: all pay
in, one name takes the pot
Motor itu tergelincir di jalan basah
dan menabrak pagar rumah.
= That motorbike skidded on the wet
road and hit the fence of a house.
Nobody skidded it. Lesson 16 taught ter-
as a state: terbuka, open; terlihat,
visible. This is its other half - the
thing that happened to you, and that you
did not do.
gelincir  ->  tergelincir  skidded
sandung   ->  tersandung   tripped
sedak     ->  tersedak     choked
dampar    ->  terdampar    washed up
tular     ->  tertular     caught it
Three you will meet in any week.
Matahari sudah terbenam.              Press 1
= The sun has already set.
Anak itu tersandung batu.             Press 2
= The child tripped on a stone.
Banyak anak tertular penyakit.        Press 3
= Many children caught the illness.
Put ter- beside meN- on one root and the
difference is a hand:
menjebak   somebody sets the trap
terjebak   he is stuck, and nobody
meant him to be
ter- says it is simply so. No hand did it,
and none is named.
